overall_summary: Bitcoin faces clear selling pressure from record ETF outflows and a hawkish Fed stance. Geopolitical tensions add risk-off sentiment across markets. Traders await resolution on support near 58K.
key_points: Record $4.5B June Bitcoin ETF outflows hit sentiment
Fed sticks to 2% target, cooling rate-cut hopes
Iran and China tensions lift geopolitical risk premium
Bitcoin rebounds toward 60K after testing 58K support
Alt ETF flows outpace Bitcoin amid mixed demand

items.title: Bitcoin Spot ETFs Post Record June Outflows of $4.5B
items.summary: U.S. Bitcoin ETFs saw their worst month on record with roughly $4.5 billion in net outflows during June, extending a multi-week streak of redemptions. The selling pressure carried into early July with another $220 million plus daily outflows reported. Traders should watch whether this institutional exit continues to weigh on spot demand and price stability.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure likely keeps BTC capped near current levels.

items.title: Bitcoin Dips Below $58K Then Rebounds Toward $60K
items.summary: BTC briefly traded under $58,000 on July 1, marking a fresh multi-month low near the 200-week moving average, before recovering above $59,000 and pushing back toward the $60,000 level. The move came amid broader macro pressures including geopolitics and ETF redemptions. Traders should monitor whether the bounce holds as a support test or gives way to further downside.
items.impact: Price consolidating near key technical levels with limited directional conviction.

items.title: Tether Freezes 131 TRON Wallets Over ISIS-K Sanctions
items.summary: Tether acted on updated U.S. sanctions by freezing 131 TRON-based wallets linked to the ISIS-K list. The move highlights ongoing compliance risks for stablecoin issuers and users on certain chains. Traders should note potential liquidity or sentiment effects on affected networks and broader stablecoin usage.
items.impact: Short-term caution on TRON and related stablecoin flows but limited direct BTC impact.

items.title: Large 1,156 BTC Whale Transfer From Coinbase Institutional
items.summary: Over 1,156 Bitcoin worth about $69 million moved from Coinbase Institutional to an unknown new wallet in a single transaction. Such large on-chain moves often signal potential distribution or custody shifts by big holders. Traders watch these flows for clues on near-term supply pressure.
items.impact: Adds to watchlist for possible selling or repositioning by large entities.

items.title: Crypto ETFs Show Mixed Flows With Alts Outpacing BTC
items.summary: While Bitcoin ETFs bled heavily, some altcoin products like XRP saw modest inflows and Solana or Hyperliquid products posted better relative performance in June. This rotation suggests institutions are selectively allocating away from BTC. Traders should track whether capital continues to rotate or returns to Bitcoin.
items.impact: Potential near-term underperformance for BTC versus select alts.

items.title: US June Jobs Report Released Amid Fed Watch
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released the June employment situation today, with nonfarm payrolls, unemployment at 4.3 percent, and average hourly earnings all in focus. Expectations pointed to softer job gains around 110,000 to 115,000 versus May's 172,000. Traders care because the data directly influences Federal Reserve rate path bets, dollar strength, bond yields, and overall risk sentiment in crypto and equities.
items.impact: Sets near-term tone for Fed policy expectations and market volatility.

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh Sticks to 2% Inflation Target
items.summary: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told a European panel he will disappoint anyone expecting tolerance for inflation above 2 percent and gave no hints on near-term policy easing. The comments came just ahead of today's jobs data. Traders should watch because they reinforce a hawkish stance that supports higher-for-longer rates, stronger dollar, and pressure on risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Bolsters higher rate expectations, weighing on risk sentiment.

items.title: Factory Orders and Auto Sales Also Due Today
items.summary: May factory orders and June auto sales figures are scheduled alongside the jobs report. These provide additional color on manufacturing and consumer demand. Markets pay attention as they round out the macro picture and can influence bond yields and dollar moves.
items.impact: Adds to today's data-driven volatility in rates and FX.

items.title: Initial Jobless Claims and Broader Labor Data
items.summary: Weekly initial claims and wage details are part of the June labor package. Steady or rising claims alongside wage growth can shift views on labor market cooling. Crypto traders monitor because softer labor signals often boost rate-cut odds and risk appetite.
items.impact: Fine-tunes Fed expectations and short-term market direction.

items.title: US-Iran Talks Advance in Doha on Hormuz, Assets
items.summary: US and Iranian officials held separate indirect talks in Qatar yesterday with mediators, agreeing to keep discussions going on implementing their memorandum of understanding. Iran is pushing hard for the US to unfreeze about six billion dollars in assets and to recognize its control over the Strait of Hormuz. Traders should watch this closely because any real progress could ease oil supply fears and support risk assets, while a stall raises escalation risks. Vice President Vance called the meetings positive.
items.impact: Potential oil price relief and risk-on sentiment if diplomacy advances.

items.title: Trump Reviews Military Options on Iran Despite Talks
items.summary: President Trump has been briefed on possible military strikes against Iran even as indirect diplomacy continues in Doha. Officials say he prefers a deal but is keeping all options open to prevent Iran from getting nuclear weapons or tightening its grip on the Strait. Markets care because any shift back toward strikes could spike oil volatility and hit risk assets hard.
items.impact: Keeps uncertainty high around energy prices and geopolitical risk premium.

items.title: Iran Demands Hormuz Sovereignty Recognition in MoU
items.summary: Tehran is insisting the US formally acknowledge its authority over the Strait of Hormuz as part of any lasting agreement. Iranian officials say they will continue collecting fees from ships and want frozen assets released to buy needed goods. A ship grounding incident in the strait yesterday highlights the ongoing tensions that directly affect global oil flows.
items.impact: Sustains oil market volatility and shipping risk premium.

items.title: Taiwan Coast Guard Warns on Chinese Vessel Incursions
items.summary: Taiwan's coast guard vowed to intervene against Chinese vessels operating near its waters, raising fresh escalation concerns in the Taiwan Strait. The move comes amid broader regional tensions and could complicate US-China relations at a sensitive time. Traders should note it adds another layer of geopolitical risk to Asia markets and supply chains.
items.impact: Adds tail risk to regional equities and semiconductor supply chains.
